tagline: Gravel around the Wilson Creek Range to a rough old town.
intro: Gravel roads circle the Wilson Creek Range, crossing wide basins and slipping through narrow canyons. Along the skirts of the range they wind through an old volcanic caldera gone over to pinyon and juniper, and toward the peaks, under Mount Wilson's 9,315-foot summit, aspen and ponderosa pine take over. Historic cabins and a pioneer cemetery turn up along the way.
Near the end of the loop comes Pioche, a silver camp that by the early 1870s was among the most important in Nevada and had a name as one of the roughest towns in the Old West.

moments.title: Spring Valley State Park
moments.text: A 1965 dam on Meadow Valley Wash holds back the 65-acre Eagle Valley Reservoir, and the park around it keeps a set of historic ranch buildings.

moments.title: Pioche
moments.text: Local lore holds that 72 men died in gunfights here before the camp saw its first natural death, and Boot Hill is still there to make the point.

practical: Parts of the byway may need a high-clearance vehicle.
